column1: # These files guard CONFIRMED security defects. JC-011 happened because a
# refactor deleted the regression suites protecting JC-005 and JC-006 and
# reintroduced both defects with nothing failing -- deleting a test never fails
# scripts/qa/check-protected-tests.sh fails CI if a listed file disappears or is
# Removing a line is a DELIBERATE, REVIEWABLE act. Do it only when the defect it
# guards is closed by design (the state is unrepresentable), never to make a
# build green. Migrating a file? Update the path here in the same commit.

column3: JC-005 assist/escalation bypass, JC-006 deactivated-actor internal notes
G-07 phone privacy enforced structurally
BR-1 matrix + current-state tripwires
BR-1 DB backstop, append-only logs, JC-010
RT-002/003/004 inverted guards: participant-set authorization, on_behalf_mode attribution
RT-005/007/008 inverted guards: signing secret, attachment validation, SYSTEM-message forgery
RT-024/025 BR-1 structural backstop, proven against the database with the application bypassed
RT-023 fresh-database acceptance: every table, FK, trigger and index a running system needs
RT-001/NF-08 closed by design: no source reads a client-supplied identity; auth refuses to start unconfigured (supersedes identity-seam.spec.ts, whose seam Phase 1 deleted)
PD-2 a parent may join a Student Group call but never start one; BR-1/C-4 still take precedence
Phase 1: a supervisor reaches only their current scope; reassignment moves access immediately; conversations, messages, search, moderation, calls, notifications and IDOR
Phase 1: login, account lifecycle, device limit, per-device and global logout, and password reset ending every session
Phase 1: cross-tenant access is blocked even for a manager; the permission table and its TypeScript mirror agree
Phase 1: role defaults and override precedence -- DENY beats ALLOW beats the role default, and an inactive actor holds nothing
Phase 1: password hashing and JWT verification -- algorithm confusion, tampering and expiry all refused
Phase 1: one live primary supervisor per family, bounded cover, guarded reassignment, scope follows the assignment
Phase 1: RLS is a live control -- proved with the application bypassed, as the authenticated role
A-7/RT-012 receipt roster is viewer-scoped; A-8/RT-006 signed URLs cannot escape their conversation; delete-for-everyone is a permission key, not a role name
Phase 1 closure: the API's connection is least-privileged and RLS actually constrains it -- proved by running the real services as chat_app
Phase 1 closure: forged and tampered tokens, revoked sessions, privilege escalation, IDOR, supervisor scope, cross-tenant access
Phase 1 closure: login and password-recovery abuse protection, and that the throttle is not itself an enumeration oracle
Phase 1 closure: a socket that loses scope stops receiving the conversation, and one whose session ends is dropped
Phase 1 deployment closure: the process refuses to start on an owner, superuser, creator or BYPASSRLS connection -- the four ways RLS is silently switched off
